# What Is an SEO GEO Agency, and How Do You Choose the Right One?


If you are evaluating GEO agencies right now, you have probably noticed something odd about the search results for that exact query. Most of the top-ranking pages are agency roundup lists. Ten agencies, brief descriptions, a comparison table, and a CTA at the bottom. The pattern repeats across every result. What none of those pages tell you is how to actually evaluate whether an agency can do the work, or whether they are selling a dashboard with a strategy deck attached.


We built[Geostar](https://www.geostar.ai/) around that distinction. Our team runs integrated GEO and SEO engagements for brands in e-commerce and SaaS, professional services, and other verticals. We write the content, implement the technical fixes, build the authority signals, and measure citation outcomes. Not as recommendations in a slide deck. As delivered work. This article is the evaluation guide we wish existed when our own clients were shopping for a partner: what a GEO SEO agency actually does, what separates real capability from repackaged SEO, and six questions that reveal whether an agency can deliver.


## What a GEO SEO Agency Actually Does


A GEO SEO agency optimizes a brand's visibility across two systems simultaneously: traditional search engines (Google, Bing) and AI-powered search platforms (ChatGPT and Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Claude). The "GEO" in the name stands for Generative Engine Optimization, the discipline of getting your brand cited and recommended in AI-generated answers.


The key word is "simultaneously." Traditional SEO agencies focus on ranking web pages for keyword-driven queries. GEO adds a different layer: making sure the brand appears when an AI system synthesizes an answer from multiple sources. The retrieval mechanism is different, the content requirements are different, and the measurement framework is different.


Executing on GEO requires combining several disciplines into one integrated strategy: SEO, digital PR, review management, content production, and distribution across multiple channels. That integration is what separates a GEO agency from a traditional SEO shop that added "AI optimization" to its services page.


A good GEO SEO agency does not treat these as separate workstreams assigned to different teams. The content strategy informs the technical implementation. The technical implementation determines what AI crawlers can parse. The authority work determines whether AI systems trust the source enough to cite it. Pulling any one of those threads without the others produces incomplete results.


For a deeper primer on the discipline itself, our[guide to Generative Engine Optimization](https://www.geostar.ai/what-is-geo) covers the foundational concepts and terminology.


## GEO vs. SEO: What Changes When You Add Generative AI


The easiest way to understand the shift is to look at what changes across each core workstream when GEO enters the engagement.


SEO is not going away. It remains the foundation: crawling and indexing, quality signals, intent matching. GEO determines which sources AI systems choose to synthesize when generating answers. The agencies producing results in 2026 run both workstreams as a single integrated program, not as separate services with separate teams.


Our[complete guide to GEO](https://www.geostar.ai/blog/complete-guide-to-generative-engine-optimization-2025) covers the technical mechanics of how AI systems select sources and what content characteristics increase citation probability.


## Why AI Search Changes the Agency Selection Calculus


Three data points frame the urgency.


First, referral traffic from large language models grew 800% between Q3 and Q4 of 2024 \[1\]. That growth rate has continued into 2025 and 2026 as AI search platforms expand their user bases and usage frequency.


Second, Gartner projects that traditional search engine volume will drop 25% by 2026, with search marketing losing share to AI chatbots and virtual agents \[2\]. That projection is playing out in real time across our client base. Brands with strong first-page rankings are watching their click-through rates compress as AI Overviews absorb the top of the SERP. A growing share of US consumers already use AI platforms as their primary discovery tool, and the trajectory is accelerating, not leveling off.


Third, the GEO services market was valued at $1.01 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $17.02 billion by 2034, according to Intel Market Research \[3\]. That trajectory reflects the scale of enterprise budget shifting toward AI visibility.


At Geostar, we see the pattern that connects all three numbers on a weekly basis. Clients come to us with solid domain authority and first-page rankings for their most important keywords. When we run their[AI visibility audit](https://www.geostar.ai/blog/impact-of-ai-on-brand-visibility) , the brand does not appear in a single AI-generated answer for those same queries.


The SEO execution is fine. The problem is that AI search uses different selection criteria, and nobody on their team was optimizing for them.


That gap is what makes agency selection different today. Hiring an SEO agency that does not also run GEO means optimizing for a search channel whose share of total discovery is shrinking, while ignoring the channel that is growing fastest.


The SERP for "GEO agency" itself illustrates the point. Search for that term and the top result is an AI Overview synthesizing advice about what to look for in a GEO partner. The blue-link results below it are roundup articles from agencies positioning themselves in the category. If your agency is not structured to earn placement in both layers of that result page, it is not built for the current search environment.


## Core Services a Real GEO SEO Agency Should Offer


The service categories below reflect what we deliver at[Geostar](https://www.geostar.ai/agency) and what we consider table stakes for any agency claiming GEO capability.


1. **Prompt-space research and query mapping.** Before any content gets written, identify which AI queries matter for the client's category. This means running actual prompts across every major AI platform, documenting which brands get cited, and mapping the competitive field of AI-generated answers.
2. **GEO and AI visibility audit.** Baseline measurement of where the brand appears and where it does not in AI-generated answers. This is the equivalent of a technical SEO audit, but for the AI layer. Without it, there is no way to prioritize work or measure progress.
3. **AI-optimized content production.** Not briefs, outlines, or recommendations — actual content that gets produced and published. The structural requirements for AI retrieval (different formatting, sourcing, and distribution than traditional SEO content) mean this work cannot be outsourced to a generic content team. We cover the mechanics in our[guide to optimizing content for AI search](https://www.geostar.ai/blog/optimizing-content-for-ai-search-optimization) .
4. **Technical GEO implementation.**[Schema markup](https://www.geostar.ai/blog/complete-guide-schema-markup-ai-search-optimization) and structured data that clarify entities for AI systems. Robots.txt configuration for AI crawlers. Server-rendered HTML for content that JavaScript-dependent crawlers cannot parse.
5. **Authority and entity building.** The most visible divergence from traditional SEO. Link building for PageRank and citation building for AI retrieval share some overlap, but they require different tactics and target different systems. Digital PR, earned media, and off-site mentions build the brand's presence in the knowledge bases AI systems draw from.
6. **GEO-specific tracking and reporting.** Citation rate, citation share, source gap analysis, and[AI-driven brand mention monitoring](https://www.geostar.ai/blog/analyzing-ai-driven-brand-mentions) . These metrics exist alongside traditional SEO reporting, not as a replacement. If an agency cannot show you where your brand appears in AI answers and how that changes over time, they are not doing GEO.
7. **Inbound channel management.** Blog, social (LinkedIn and Reddit), and emerging AI-native surfaces. Where AI systems discover sources matters as much as what those sources say, so distribution is not an afterthought.


The throughline is execution. We do not deliver the brief and hand it off. Content gets written and published, then monitored. Technical fixes get implemented. Authority campaigns get run. The distinction matters because the majority of vendors in this category sell monitoring and recommendations, not delivery.


## How to Evaluate a GEO SEO Agency: Six Questions That Reveal Competence


Most buyers evaluate agencies based on case studies and pricing. Those inputs matter, but they do not tell you whether the agency can actually execute GEO work. These six questions do.


1. **Do they measure AI visibility separately from search rankings, or bundle them together?**A real GEO program tracks citation rate, mention frequency, and source position in AI-generated answers as distinct metrics. If the agency reports "AI optimization" as a line item inside their standard SEO dashboard, they are likely running the same playbook with a new label.
2. **Who does the content work: in-house writers and editors, or white-label outsourcing?**GEO content requires specific structural decisions (entity markup, citation-ready formatting, query-answer alignment) that generic freelance writers do not make by default. Ask to see their content team's workflow and the editorial process behind it.
3. **Can they show you a prompt-space audit from a real engagement?**The prompt-space audit is the GEO equivalent of a keyword research report. It maps which AI queries the client needs to win, which brands currently get cited for those queries, and where the gaps are. If the agency has not built this artifact for a client, they are not running a GEO program.
4. **How do they track citation outcomes vs. platform mentions?**Citations (linked source attributions) and mentions (unlinked brand references) require different tactics to earn and serve different strategic purposes. A citation means an AI system selected your content as a source and linked to it. A mention means the AI named your brand without linking. Both are valuable; both are measurable. An agency that conflates them is missing half the measurement picture.
5. **Do they have GEO-specific case studies, or SEO case studies they have relabeled?**Look for results described in GEO terms: citation rate improvement, mention frequency growth, source position changes. If every case study is framed as "organic traffic growth" or "ranking improvements," the GEO work may be cosmetic. Ask what changed in the AI answers after their engagement started. A real GEO agency can answer that question with specific data.
6. **How do they handle the gap between traditional SEO foundations and AI-specific optimization?**Some agencies specialize in GEO monitoring but do not touch the SEO foundation. Others run traditional SEO and bolt on "AI readiness" as an upsell. The best outcome is a single integrated engagement where both workstreams inform each other. Ask how their SEO work feeds their GEO strategy, and vice versa. If they cannot describe the connection, the integration is likely surface-level.


One pattern we see from clients who have been through a bad agency experience: the previous vendor rebranded their existing SEO playbook as GEO without adding PR, authority building, or AI-specific measurement. The content looked the same, the reporting looked the same, and the only difference was new terminology on the invoice.


The cost of that mistake is time. GEO gains compound. Brands that establish citation presence early build a structural advantage as AI systems reinforce their source preferences over repeated queries. Six months with a repackaged SEO vendor is six months of lost citation momentum that a competitor was accumulating.


That is the red flag these six questions are designed to catch.

## FAQ


**What is GEO SEO?**


GEO SEO refers to the practice of optimizing a website for both traditional search engines and AI-powered search platforms. SEO handles the ranking foundations: crawlability, content quality, link signals. GEO handles the AI visibility layer: getting cited in ChatGPT and Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Claude. The two disciplines share a foundation but require different content strategies and technical implementations, with separate measurement frameworks.


**Is GEO going to replace SEO?**


No. GEO and SEO are complementary. SEO remains the foundation for crawling and indexing, for quality signals. GEO determines which sources AI systems synthesize when generating answers. The brands performing best in 2026 run both as a single integrated program. Pausing SEO to "pivot to GEO" is a mistake; the technical and content work that earns traditional rankings also feeds AI source selection.


**How much does an SEO agency cost?**


Agency pricing varies widely based on scope and engagement model. Traditional SEO retainers for mid-market companies typically range from $3,000 to $15,000 per month. GEO adds workstreams (prompt-space research, AI visibility auditing, citation tracking, authority building) that increase the scope of work. At Geostar, we do not publish pricing. Every engagement starts with a[free audit](https://www.geostar.ai/contact) that scopes the work to the client's specific situation.


**What is a GEO agency?**


A GEO agency specializes in Generative Engine Optimization: helping brands get cited and recommended in AI-generated search answers. The best GEO agencies also maintain traditional SEO expertise, because the two disciplines share technical foundations and content infrastructure. The key differentiator is whether the agency measures and optimizes for AI-specific outcomes (citation rate, mention frequency, source position) rather than only tracking traditional rankings.


**How long does GEO take to show results?**


Most GEO programs begin showing measurable citation changes within 60 to 90 days, depending on the client's starting authority and the competitive density of their category. Initial audit and strategy work takes two to four weeks. Content and technical execution begins producing citation movement within the first quarter.


Unlike SEO, where ranking changes can take six to twelve months, AI systems update their source pools more frequently, so new content can earn citations faster than it would earn first-page rankings.


**Should I pause SEO to focus on GEO?**


No. The foundations that drive SEO performance (site structure, content quality, domain authority) are the same signals that feed the AI retrieval pipeline. Stopping SEO work degrades both channels. The right approach is running both as a single program where improvements in one workstream strengthen the other.
